data.name: Marwaah
data.gender_notes: Marwaah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'Marwah', meaning 'graceful' or 'tender'. In Islamic tradition, Marwaah is the name of a woman mentioned in the Hadith who offered water to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) during his journey from Makkah to Madinah. The name Marwaah carries the meaning “Graceful, Tender” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu. Parents who choose Marwaah usually hope their child will grow to embody graceful, tender and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes kindness, compassion, and nurturing qualities. It is believed that a child named Marwaah will grow up to be a gentle and loving individual.
data.etymology: Marwaah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Graceful, Tender.”
